title: Jimmy Harris: OU's Unbeaten QB Who Became an Oilman
question: What did Oklahoma quarterback Jimmy Harris do after football?
answer: Jimmy Harris, who quarterbacked Oklahoma from 1954 to 1956 without ever losing, played four pro seasons as a defensive back. He then earned a geology degree and worked in the oil business from 1962 on, running Midroc Operating Company.
summary: Jimmy Harris led OU to back-to-back national titles in 1955 and 1956 without a loss, then played in the pros and built a long career in the oil business.
body: Jimmy Harris never lost a game as Oklahoma's quarterback. He took over in the 1954 season and played through 1956, and the Sooners won national championships in 1955 and 1956 during Bud Wilkinson's famous 47-game winning streak. The Philadelphia Inquirer's obituary credits him with a 25-0 record as a starter, and ESPN Classic noted that OU went 31-0 over his three seasons.

He also played defense and returned punts, and Philadelphia drafted him in the fifth round. Harris played four seasons in the pros as a defensive back, with the Eagles in 1957, the Rams in 1958, the Dallas Texans in 1960 and the Cowboys in 1961, finishing with 11 interceptions.

Football was not his long-term plan. In a 2003 ESPN Classic interview, Harris explained that players of his day needed degrees because early pro pay was small. He had roughnecked in the summers for Roy Guffey, an OU player from the 1920s, and got interested in the oil business. After the Rams offered him less than he wanted, he asked Wilkinson for advice, and the coach told him to finish his geology degree. Harris also spent one year on Wilkinson's OU staff, in 1959.
He said he had been in the oil business since 1962 and ran Midroc Operating Company. Harris died of lung cancer on August 9, 2011, in Shreveport, Louisiana, at age 76.
